# SB-1015: Safety bulletin: noise exposure
Revision: Rev D
Plant: P3, line P3-L2
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses elevated noise exposures associated with the heat treat area adjacent to the Ring Rolling process served by EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Background investigations and employee feedback indicate that troubleshooting, maintenance activities, and process upsets in the heat treat cell can produce impulsive and sustained noise levels that increase the risk of hearing injury and reduce communication clarity for operators and maintenance technicians. Contributing factors include open access during loading and unloading sequences, compressed air use for part handling, and metal-to-metal impact noise during improper quench sequencing. Noise sources are intermittent and can be amplified by the cell geometry and adjacent conveyor systems. In addition to direct auditory risk, elevated noise complicates the identification of equipment faults, which can delay corrective action and prolong exposure.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Ring Rolling heat treat furnace equipment identified as EQ-P3-L2-HT03 located on line P3-L2 at Plant P3. It also applies to tasks performed in the immediate work zone during loading, unloading, quench handling, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance when workers are expected to be within the noise field generated by EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Refer to MM-P3-L2-HT03 for machine maintenance requirements and SB-1041 for related hearing protection program expectations. For engineering change implications, see ECN-2026-017.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Ensure acoustic barriers and full enclosures are installed and maintained per design drawings referenced in ECN-2026-017. Barriers must be in place during normal operation and immediately reinstalled after maintenance to prevent sound leakage into the workplace.
- Confirm quench sequencing controls are set and verified prior to production startup. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. This limit is to prevent extended exposure to impact and splashing noise from delayed quench events and to ensure consistent process timing that reduces the likelihood of secondary handling that generates noise.

Administrative controls
- Limit personnel access to the immediate work zone during known high-noise activities by using the line P3-L2 access control procedures and signage. When troubleshooting or adjustments must be performed, designate a single, trained performer when practicable and schedule work to minimize concurrent noisy tasks.
- Implement a mandatory pre-task briefing for non-routine interventions in the EQ-P3-L2-HT03 zone that includes planned duration, expected noise sources, and required protective measures. Briefings must reference MM-P3-L2-HT03 for lockout/tagout and safe isolation steps.

Personal protective equipment
- Use the hearing protection devices and wearing criteria established in SB-1041 for the heat treat area. Replace disposable inserts and cushions per supplier guidance and records in MM-P3-L2-HT03. Selection should prioritize both attenuation and the ability to maintain communication during critical steps.

Monitoring and verification
- Conduct periodic noise assessments whenever process changes are implemented or after mechanical repairs that could alter acoustic characteristics. Findings and corrective actions must be recorded and retained with the equipment maintenance file referenced in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Use supervisor observations, employee reports, and the records noted below to verify that engineering and administrative controls remain effective. Follow-up measurements should be scheduled after any event that exceeds expected acoustic behavior or after the actions documented in ECN-2026-017 are performed.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for the quench delay limit: extended delay between transfer and quench causes operators to intervene in non-standard ways to stabilize parts, increasing handling noise and creating impact events as parts shift. Limiting delay to the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds reduces transient noise and minimizes opportunities for manual intervention that elevate exposure.
- Example scenario A: During a transfer command failure, parts remained in the transfer position. With the delay limit enforced and an immediate automated fallback, the system completed quench within the prescribed delay and avoided additional handling. Administrative controls ensured only one technician entered the zone to reset commands, wearing hearing protection per SB-1041.
- Example scenario B: During preventive maintenance, acoustic barrier panels were removed for access but not reinstalled. Work planning per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and this bulletin required temporary barriers and signage. The combination of administrative control and PPE maintained acceptable exposure while the panels were refitted.

Records to keep
- Noise assessment reports and measurement data for EQ-P3-L2-HT03, retained with the maintenance records in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Pre-task briefings and authorization forms for interventions in the heat treat zone, filed with the line P3-L2 job safety records.
- Corrective action documentation following any event that triggers a review, including references to applicable design or change documents such as ECN-2026-017.
- Hearing protection issue and replacement logs, consistent with the practices in SB-1041.

Effective date
Effective date: upon release of this bulletin.

References
- ECN-2026-017
- MM-P3-L2-HT03
- SB-1041

Distribution and responsibilities
Supervisors on line P3-L2 are responsible for ensuring compliance with the controls in this bulletin and for maintaining the records noted above. Maintenance leads must coordinate with engineering to verify that any changes outlined in ECN-2026-017 do not compromise the acoustic controls. Safety personnel will audit compliance and support noise assessments and training aligned with SB-1041.
